clue.text: Fliers qualified to wear soldier's decorations

indicators.note: what a person wears goes around them, so the soldier's letters enclose the others

parts.note: GI is the usual word for an American soldier
the Royal Air Force, Britain's fliers
fit for a job, suitably qualified

explanation.surface: Pilots who have earned the right display medals on a soldier's uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decorations' looks like medals, but it means daubed wall art; the soldier's GI is split to hold the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti is scrawled or painted ornament on walls, a kind of (unofficial) decoration.

clue.text: Active resistance intercepts agent

indicators.note: to intercept is to get in the way, so one letter sits in the middle of the other word

parts.note: a secret agent
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A lively resistance fighter stops an enemy agent in his tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry describes someone nimble and lively, especially an older person who stays energetic.

clue.text: Harry Potter possibly is in favour of turning up at Hollywood awards night, initially

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: The boy wizard supports turning up at an Oscars ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Potter's parents were killed when he was a baby, so he is one example; 'possibly' flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Potter lost both parents as an infant, making him a child without parents, an example of the word.

clue.text: Got a hundred pounds to guard empty residence

indicators.note: guarding something means surrounding it, so the money word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
quid is British slang for pounds sterling

indicators.note: an empty word has lost its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of residence

explanation.surface: Someone obtained a hundred pounds to protect a vacant house.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is everyday British slang for a pound (or pounds) of money.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to obtain or get it, so acquired is a past-tense synonym of got.

clue.text: Cancel Levant aid I arranged

indicators.note: arranged suggests letters being set out in a new order

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An order to call off a relief package organised for the Eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: The Levant is the historic name for the eastern Mediterranean coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To invalidate something is to make it void, which is to cancel or annul it.

clue.text: Flight delay causes travel sickness

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft, taken here as a flight
a lag is a delay or time gap

explanation.surface: A late plane leaves passengers feeling queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight delay' reads as a single complaint about a late plane, but its two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet lag is the fatigue and disorientation felt after crossing time zones, a malady caused by travel.

clue.text: Ready peeled in advance

parts.note: pre- is the prefix for beforehand, and it comes first here
pared means trimmed or peeled, as with fruit

explanation.surface: Vegetables already peeled ahead of time, ready to cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in advance' both supplies its letters and tells you they go in front of the other piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prepared is made ready beforehand, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: He is full of energy — for Monday, anyway

indicators.note: anyway read as 'any way' says the letters may be put in any order

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A man bursting with vigour even at the start of the working week.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo is a generator, and figuratively a tirelessly energetic person.

clue.text: Stop party for foreigners held in unfinished room

indicators.note: being held in something means sitting inside it
something unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
the African National Congress, a party abroad rather than at home

explanation.surface: A call to halt a gathering of overseas visitors kept in a half-built room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party for foreigners' means a foreign political party: the ANC of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: To cancel is to call off or put a stop to something planned.

clue.text: Uncertain whether family has lost heart

parts.note: if can mean whether, as in 'ask if'

indicators.note: losing the heart strips out the inside, so only the outer letters remain

parts.note: the first and last letters of family

explanation.surface: Doubting whether a family has become disheartened.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is an informal word for doubtful or questionable, so it matches uncertain.

clue.text: Hard on this paper's expert to be principled

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
taken as written
from the newspaper's own point of view, its things are ours
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: The newspaper's specialist is told off for not being ethical enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This paper's' is the setter speaking as the Guardian, so it gives OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An honourable person acts according to moral principles, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Deny any connection with Sid's returning to confess

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the name is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning round
to own up is to confess

explanation.surface: Sid comes back to admit his guilt and rejects all ties.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown someone is to refuse to acknowledge any relationship with them.

clue.text: Work I've found boxing papers is burdensome

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so these letters go around the next piece

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
taken as written without the apostrophe
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Someone finds their job of sorting newspapers into boxes a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: Work and I've join, then that pair encloses the newspapers word.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppressive means weighing heavily on someone, harsh or hard to bear, as burdensome does.

clue.text: Union anger over opening of investigation following damage

indicators.note: following says this group comes after the damage word

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage

indicators.note: one word placed over another covers it, so the anger word goes round the single letter

parts.note: rage is fierce anger

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of investigation

explanation.surface: A trade union furious about an inquiry into harm done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' suggests a trade union, but it is a wedding; the single letter slips in after the first letter of the anger word.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage is the legal joining of two people, a union in the matrimonial sense.

clue.text: Obstruct international politician joining journalist going to Europe

parts.note: I is a standard abbreviation for international
a Member of Parliament
ed is short for editor
E is the abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: A global politician teams up with a reporter heading to the Continent to block something.
explanation.definitionFit: To impede is to hinder or block progress, the same as to obstruct.

clue.text: Reps said doctor is without hope

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, altering the order of these letters

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Sales reps report that the physician has given up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like the person who is hopeless, but it is a verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to lose all hope, so despairs fits the verb phrase is without hope.

clue.text: Ladies could be perfect examples

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might take another form when rearranged

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Women who might serve as models of perfection.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are standards of perfection or models worth imitating.

clue.text: Scandalous counterfeit drug for flu, perhaps

parts.note: a sham is a fake

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word may appear in a different arrangement of its letters

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Selling a fake medicine as an influenza cure is outrageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Shameful conduct brings disgrace, and scandalous is a near-synonym for disgraceful.

clue.text: Guidance from daddy regularly at fault

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of daddy
a vice is a moral fault or failing

explanation.surface: Tips from a father who is often in the wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice is counsel or recommendation, the same thing as guidance.

clue.text: Upset after princess removed under pressure

indicators.note: something removed is taken away, so those letters come out of the word

parts.note: distressed means upset
Princess Diana was known as Di

explanation.surface: Someone was upset after a royal was taken away while under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: Di was the popular name of Diana, Princess of Wales; removing her from the front of the upset word leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stressed means suffering mental strain or tension, the state of being under pressure.

clue.text: Up to about an hour of excitement

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: till means until, up to a time
hr is the abbreviation for hour

explanation.surface: Up to sixty minutes or so of exhilaration.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden feeling of excitement or pleasure.

clue.text: Despicable person finally bought old English newspaper

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the last letter of bought
O is the abbreviation for old
E is the abbreviation for English
a rag is a disparaging word for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A contemptible man at last purchased a long-established English paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Toerag is British slang for a contemptible rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Toerag is British slang insult for a scoundrel, someone worthless and despised.

clue.text: Shake up capital after tax rebate starts

indicators.note: after places the city word second, behind the tax initials
starts are the first letters of the words before it

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means reading the word from bottom to top

parts.note: the Italian capital city

explanation.surface: Shake up the capital city after tax refunds begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shake up' reads as a phrasal verb, but the definition stops at 'Shake'; 'up' turns the city round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a trembling or slight earthquake, a shake as a noun.

clue.text: Reform he is absurd to ignore

indicators.note: to reform something is to shape it again, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: He says reform is a ridiculous thing to overlook.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush aside a point is to dismiss it without consideration, effectively to disregard it.

clue.text: Middle-age regret reportedly increased

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of age

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Regret about middle age apparently grew over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middle-age' looks like a life stage, but it asks for the middle of the word age.
explanation.definitionFit: Grew is the past tense of grow, meaning became larger, so it matches increased.

clue.text: It's involved in developing amenities for sport

indicators.note: being involved in something means being caught up within it, here within the letters of the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something is part of building new facilities for athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: A game is a sporting contest or competitive pastime, an instance of sport.

clue.text: Intelligent Catholic has the means to gain an advantage

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Catholic

parts.words: the means to gain an advantage
parts.note: a lever is something used to gain leverage, an advantage

explanation.surface: A smart Catholic knows how to get the upper hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever means quick-witted and bright, a synonym of intelligent.

clue.text: Giant turns sour on me

indicators.note: turns suggests letters being twisted round into a new order

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A giant becomes hostile towards the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Giant' looks like a noun for an ogre, but it is the adjective meaning huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Enormous means extremely large, and giant used as an adjective means the same.
